key_insight: Ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification raised hardness in Cr3C2–NiCr coatings, but the response depended strongly on deposition route and treatment settings.
engineering_relevance: For wear-resistant thermal-sprayed coatings, UNSM can improve local mechanical performance, yet process optimization must be tailored separately for detonation-sprayed and HVOF deposits.
method: Compared detonation-sprayed and HVOF Cr3C2–NiCr coatings after UNSM.
Varied static load (20, 30 N) and vibration amplitude (20, 30 μm) across four treated samples per route.
Measured hardness with nanoindentation-like instrumental testing at 300 mN and examined post-scratch SEM morphology.
evidence_signal: Hardness ranged from 820–970 HV for DS samples and 546–1165 HV for HVOF samples, with the highest values at DS-T1 (20 N/20 μm) and HVOF-T4 (30 N/30 μm).
watch_item: Scratch SEM showed crack-like discontinuities, but the study does not clearly separate UNSM-induced effects from scratch damage or establish a definitive scratch-resistance ranking.
paper_title: HARDNESS AND POST-SCRATCH SURFACE MORPHOLOGY OF Cr₃C₂–NiCr COATINGS AFTER ULTRASONIC NANOCRYSTAL SURFACE MODIFICATION
